chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who accuses his wife of adultery, he said: He is flogged, then they are separated, and he does not perform li'an with her until he says: I bear witness that I saw you doing such and such.

key_terms.يُلَاعِنُهَا: he performs li'an with her (mutual imprecation/oath)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between li'an and simple accusation of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar, this hadith clarifies the distinction between li'an (mutual imprecation) and simple separation (talaq) when a husband accuses his wife of zina without the formal four-oath ritual. It establishes that mere accusation results in flogging and separation, whereas the specific legal consequences of li'an require explicit testimony of witnessing the act, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on evidentiary precision in marital disputes.
